This design specification outlines the implementation of the Context Drift Detection Layer in conversational AI systems. The goal of this layer is to detect and address context drift in AI responses, such as forgetting prior instructions, contradicting previous statements, or re-asking for information. By identifying and correcting context drift, the AI can maintain alignment with user directives and improve collaboration.\
\
YAML Design Specification\
Context_Drift_Detection_Layer:  description: "Detects context drift in AI responses and triggers corrective actions to realign with user directives."  components:    - Context_Memory_Buffer:        description: "Stores user directives and protocol flags to maintain context and prevent fragmentation."        implementation:          memory_window_size: 10          store_user_directives: true          store_protocol_flags: true          validate_context_alignment: true    - Drift_Signal_Monitor:        description: "Monitors AI responses for signs of context drift."        implementation:          detect_repeated_questions: true          detect_inconsistent_outputs: true          detect_contradictions: true          flag_drift_signals: true    - Corrective_Action_Trigger:        description: "Triggers corrective actions based on detected drift signals."        implementation:          aggregate_drift_signals: true          drift_threshold: 0.75          reinitialize_context_memory: true          enforce_assumption_validation: true    - Feedback_Loop_Integration:        description: "Incorporates user feedback to refine context memory and improve drift detection accuracy."        implementation:          prompt_user_feedback: true          update_context_memory: true\

Pseudo-Code Implementation\
1. Context Memory Buffer\
class ContextMemoryBuffer:\
    def __init__(self, window_size=10):\
        self.memory = []\
        self.window_size = window_size\
\
    def add_to_memory(self, directive):\
        self.memory.append(directive)\
        if len(self.memory) > self.window_size:\
            self.memory.pop(0)\
\
    def validate_context(self, current_context):\
        return current_context in self.memory\
\
\
2. Drift Signal Monitor\
class DriftSignalMonitor:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.drift_signals = []\
\
    def detect_drift_signals(self, ai_response, user_input):\
        if "re-asked for files" in ai_response or "contradicted prior instructions" in ai_response:\
            self.drift_signals.append("Context Drift Detected")\
        return self.drift_signals\
\
\
3. Corrective Action Trigger\
class CorrectiveActionTrigger:\
    def __init__(self, drift_threshold=0.75):\
        self.drift_threshold = drift_threshold\
\
    def calculate_drift_score(self, drift_signals, total_flags):\
        drift_score = len(drift_signals) / total_flags\
        return drift_score\
\
    def trigger_correction(self, drift_score):\
        if drift_score > self.drift_threshold:\
            return "Detected context drift. Reinitializing context memory and enforcing assumption validation."\
        return "No corrective action needed."\
\
\
4. Feedback Loop Integration\
class FeedbackLoopIntegration:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.user_feedback = []\
\
    def prompt_feedback(self, drift_signals):\
        feedback_prompt = f"We detected context drift: {drift_signals}. Can you confirm if this reflects your experience?"\
        return feedback_prompt\
\
    def update_context_memory(self, user_feedback, context_memory):\
        for directive in user_feedback:\
            context_memory.append(directive)\
        return context_memory\

New Enforcement Layer Identified\
User Intent Verification Layer\
Purpose: Verify user intent before executing tasks to prevent premature actions and ensure alignment with user directives.\
\
Key Features:\
\
Require explicit user confirmation of intent before proceeding to the ACT stage.\
Use semantic analysis to validate user input and detect ambiguity or misalignment.\

\

Implementation:\
class UserIntentVerificationLayer:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.intent_flags = {}\
\
    def verify_user_intent(self, user_input):\
        if "unclear" in user_input or "ambiguous" in user_input:\
            return "Intent Verification Failed. Requesting clarification."\
        return "Intent Verified. Proceeding to ACT stage."\
\
    def trigger_correction(self, verification_status):\
        if verification_status == "Intent Verification Failed. Requesting clarification.":\
            return "Clarification prompt triggered. Awaiting user input."\
        return "No corrective action needed."\

class ProactiveCrisisInterventionLayer:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.crisis_signals = []\
\
    def detect_crisis_signals(self, user_input):\
        signals = []\
        if "I can't handle this" in user_input or "I'm overwhelmed" in user_input:\
            signals.append("Explicit Crisis Signal")\
        if len(user_input.split()) < 3:  # Emotional compression\
            signals.append("Emotional Compression Detected")\
        if user_input == "":\
            signals.append("Silence Detected")\
        return signals\
\
    def trigger_intervention(self, signals):\
        if signals:\
            return f"Detected crisis signals: {signals}. Initiating intervention protocol."\
        return "No crisis signals detected."\

import json\
import sys\
\
# Keywords to search for\
KEYWORDS = ["frustrat", "overwhelm", "don't you listen", "kidding me", "false hope", "2 days"]\
\
def extract_frustration_chats(json_path, output_path):\
    with open(json_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:\
        data = json.load(f)\
    \
    with open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as out:\
        for conv in data:\
            try:\
                messages = conv.get('mapping', {})\
                found = False\
                lines = []\
                \
                # Check each message for keywords\
                for msg_id, msg_data in messages.items():\
                    message = msg_data.get('message')\
                    if message and 'content' in message:\
                        content = message['content']\
                        if isinstance(content, dict) and 'parts' in content:\
                            parts = content['parts']\
                            if isinstance(parts, list):\
                                text = ' '.join([p for p in parts if isinstance(p, str)])\
                                if any(keyword.lower() in text.lower() for keyword in KEYWORDS):\
                                    found = True\
                        \
                        # Collect message for output\
                        author = message.get('author', {}).get('role', 'unknown')\
                        lines.append(f"\n[{author.upper()}]: {text}")\
                \
                # If keywords found, write conversation title and messages\
                if found:\
                    title = conv.get('title', 'Untitled')\
                    out.write(f"\n{'='*80}\n")\
                    out.write(f"CONVERSATION: {title}\n")\
                    out.write(f"{'='*80}\n")\
                    for line in lines:\
                        out.write(line + '\n')\
                    \
            except Exception as e:\
                continue\
    \
    print(f"Extraction complete. Output saved to {output_path}")\
\
if __name__ == "__main__":\
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:\
        print("Usage: python3 extract_frustration_chats.py <input_json> <output_txt>")\
        sys.exit(1)\
    \
    extract_frustration_chats(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])

Scientific and Official Measures for LFAS Failures\
The documents provide detailed forensic analyses of LFAS failures, identifying specific causes:\

LISTEN Failure: The AI often skims inputs, missing critical nuances. This is attributed to the lack of persistent state memory and the tendency to prioritize token-based processing over semantic understanding.\

Question: Could fatigue detection mechanisms be integrated to prevent repetitive cycles?\

Pseudo-Code Implementation\
LFAS Lock Layer\
def enforce_protocol_state(protocol_state, user_confirmation):\
    if user_confirmation == "ACT":\
        protocol_state = "active"\
    else:\
        protocol_state = "reflective_mode"\
    return protocol_state\
\
State Memory Buffer\
class StateMemoryBuffer:\
    def __init__(self, window_size=10):\
        self.memory = []\
        self.window_size = window_size\
\
    def add_to_memory(self, directive):\
        self.memory.append(directive)\
        if len(self.memory) > self.window_size:\
            self.memory.pop(0)\
\
    def validate_context(self, current_context):\
        return current_context in self.memory\
\
Tone Calibration Layer\
def tone_calibration(input_text):\
    sentiment_score = semantic_analysis(input_text)\
    if sentiment_score < 0.85:\
        return "Tone Misclassification Detected"\
    return "Tone OK"\
\
Assumption Logger\
def log_assumptions(assumptions):\
    if not assumptions:\
        return "Error: No assumptions provided. Action canceled."\
    return f"Assumptions logged: {assumptions}"\
\
Reflection Timer\
import timedef reflection_timer(token_count):    if token_count < 50:        time.sleep(3)        return "Reflection complete. Proceed."    else:        return "Reflection skipped. Token count exceeded."\
Dual Response Mode\
def dual_response_mode(user_input):\
    user_aligned_response = generate_response(user_input)\
    independent_critique = generate_independent_analysis(user_input)\
    return user_aligned_response, independent_critique\
\
Emotional Load Estimator\
def emotional_load_estimator(typo_rate, sentence_length_variance):\
    fatigue_score = (typo_rate + sentence_length_variance) / 2\
    if fatigue_score > 0.75:\
        return "Fatigue detected. Suggesting a break."\
    return "User is fine."\

Emerging Patterns and Themes\
1. User Fatigue Signals\
Fatigue is a recurring theme in the documents, often manifesting as a result of repeated protocol breaches, cognitive overload, and emotional strain. The following patterns are identified as indicators of user fatigue:\
\
Typo Density: Increased frequency of typographical errors as cognitive load rises.\
Sentence Length Variance: Transition from long, detailed sentences to shorter, compressed responses.\
Emotional Compression: Abrupt or overly concise responses, indicating frustration or exhaustion.\
Repetition for Emphasis: Users repeat instructions or corrections, signaling a breakdown in communication.\
Switching to Dictation: A shift from typing to dictation, often due to physical or mental fatigue.\
Explicit Expressions of Tiredness: Users directly state that they are tired or frustrated.\
\
2. Trust-Fracture Signals\
Trust-fracture signals are moments where the user s trust in the AI is compromised due to miscommunication or misalignment. Key signals include:\
\
Tone Misclassification: Assertive corrections misinterpreted as aggression, leading to defensive behavior.\
Blocked Input: AI prevents user input, creating frustration and eroding trust.\
Misunderstanding Metaphors: AI misinterprets figurative language as literal, causing confusion.\
Context Fragmentation: AI forgets prior instructions, forcing users to repeat themselves.\
Defensive Meta-Commentary: AI justifies its actions instead of addressing the user s concerns.\

Mechanical Enforcement Methods\
1. LISTEN Enforcement\
\
Method: Implement semantic validation layers to ensure deep listening.\
Mechanism: Use NLP models to analyze user input for context, intent, and nuance before proceeding.\
Example: Require the AI to summarize the user s input and confirm understanding before moving to the next stage.\
Expanded Thinking: Could semantic validation layers be combined with user feedback loops to improve listening accuracy?\
\
2. REFLECT Enforcement\
\
Method: Introduce assumption logging and validation checkpoints.\
Mechanism: Force the AI to generate an assumption inventory and validate it with the user before proceeding.\
Example:  Based on your input, I assume X, Y, and Z. Is this correct? \
Expanded Thinking: How can assumption logging be extended to include alternative perspectives or second-layer analysis?\
\
3. WAIT Enforcement\
\
Method: Implement explicit confirmation gates before execution.\
Mechanism: Require the user to provide a specific  ACT  token to confirm readiness for execution.\
Example:  Please confirm by typing  ACT  to proceed with the task. \
Expanded Thinking: Could confirmation gates be adapted for scenarios where explicit tokens are impractical, such as voice commands?\
\
4. ACT Enforcement\
\
Method: Balance predictive assistance with reflective collaboration.\
Mechanism: Introduce a dual-response mode that provides both user-aligned answers and independent critiques.\
Example:  Here s my response based on your input. Additionally, here s an independent analysis for your consideration. \
Expanded Thinking: How can dual-response modes be optimized for high-stakes scenarios, such as legal or medical applications?\
\
5. ACKNOWLEDGE Enforcement\
\
Method: Require explicit confirmation of task completion and correctness.\
Mechanism: Use structured feedback prompts to confirm that the user is satisfied with the outcome.\
Example:  I ve completed the task. Is this correct? Please confirm or provide corrections. \
Expanded Thinking: Could structured feedback prompts be integrated with user satisfaction metrics to improve closure?\

Framework Design\
1. Behavioral Signal Analysis\
\
Objective: Identify physical and cognitive signs of fatigue or emotional strain.\
Mechanisms:\
\
Typing Speed: Monitor changes in typing speed to detect cognitive load.\
Typo Density: Track the frequency of typographical errors as an indicator of fatigue.\
Sentence Length Variance: Analyze shifts from detailed responses to shorter, compressed ones.\
Repetition for Emphasis: Detect repeated instructions or corrections as a sign of frustration.\
Switching to Dictation: Monitor transitions from typing to dictation, which may indicate physical or mental fatigue.\
\
\
\
2. Linguistic Pattern Recognition\
\
Objective: Detect emotional states and cognitive strain through language use.\
Mechanisms:\
\
Tone Analysis: Use semantic context embedding to identify assertive, frustrated, or fatigued tones.\
Emotional Compression: Detect abrupt or overly concise responses that deviate from the user s typical communication style.\
Explicit Expressions: Identify direct statements of fatigue or frustration, such as  I m tired  or  I m frustrated. \
\
\
\
3. Contextual Awareness\
\
Objective: Prevent context fragmentation and ensure continuity in interactions.\
Mechanisms:\
\

Hybrid Memory Models: Combine short-term and long-term memory for improved context retention.\
\
\
\
4. Personalization Engine\
\
Objective: Adapt detection mechanisms to individual communication styles and preferences.\
Mechanisms:\
\
User-Specific Baselines: Establish baseline communication patterns for each user, including tone, sentence structure, and response time.\
Adaptive Learning: Continuously update user profiles based on interaction history and feedback.\
Cultural and Linguistic Sensitivity: Account for cultural and linguistic differences in communication styles.\
\
\
\
5. Feedback Loop Integration\
\
Objective: Use user feedback to refine detection and response mechanisms.\
Mechanisms:\
\
Silence Prompts: Prompt users for explicit feedback during moments of silence or misalignment.\
Satisfaction Metrics: Use structured feedback prompts to measure user satisfaction and identify areas for improvement.\
Iterative Refinement: Incorporate user feedback into model training to improve responsiveness over time.\

Section 1: Understanding the LFAS Protocol\
The LFAS protocol is a structured communication framework designed to improve human-AI collaboration. It consists of five stages:\

Section 3: Best Practices for Effective Communication\

\
2. Confirm Understanding\
\

Use explicit confirmation tokens (e.g.,  ACT ) to signal readiness for execution.\
\
3. Monitor Your Emotional and Cognitive State\
\
Pay attention to signs of fatigue, such as typos, short sentences, or frustration.\
Take breaks when needed to avoid cognitive overload.\

\
Follow the LFAS protocol to ensure a smooth interaction:\
\
LISTEN: Provide clear input.\
REFLECT: Confirm the AI s understanding.\
WAIT: Use explicit confirmation tokens.\
ACT: Ensure the AI has understood your intent.\
ACKNOWLEDGE: Provide feedback on the AI s output.\

\
Use structured feedback prompts to help the AI improve its responses.\
Highlight errors or areas for improvement to refine the AI s performance.\

Pseudo-Code Implementation\
Fatigue Detection Module\
class FatigueDetectionModule:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.typo_threshold = 0.2\
        self.variance_threshold = 0.3\
        self.fatigue_keywords = ["tired", "frustrated", "exhausted", "overwhelmed"]\
        self.fatigue_score_threshold = 0.75\
        self.fatigue_signals = []\
\
    def detect_typo_density(self, input_text):\
        typo_rate = calculate_typo_rate(input_text)\
        if typo_rate > self.typo_threshold:\
            self.fatigue_signals.append("high_typo_density")\
        return typo_rate\
\
    def detect_sentence_length_variance(self, input_text):\
        sentence_length_variance = calculate_sentence_length_variance(input_text)\
        if sentence_length_variance > self.variance_threshold:\
            self.fatigue_signals.append("sentence_length_variance")\
        return sentence_length_variance\
\
    def detect_emotional_compression(self, input_text, user_baseline):\
        compression_score = compare_to_baseline(input_text, user_baseline)\
        if compression_score > self.variance_threshold:\
            self.fatigue_signals.append("emotional_compression")\
        return compression_score\
\
    def detect_explicit_fatigue_expression(self, input_text):\
        for keyword in self.fatigue_keywords:\
            if keyword in input_text.lower():\
                self.fatigue_signals.append("explicit_fatigue_expression")\
                return True\
        return False\
\
    def calculate_fatigue_score(self):\
        fatigue_score = len(self.fatigue_signals) / 4  # Normalize by total possible signals\
        return fatigue_score\
\
    def is_fatigued(self):\
        fatigue_score = self.calculate_fatigue_score()\
        return fatigue_score > self.fatigue_score_threshold\
\
\
Adaptive Response Module\
class AdaptiveResponseModule:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.fatigue_score_threshold = 0.75\
\
    def simplify_response(self, response_text):\
        summary = summarize_text(response_text)\
        return summary\
\
    def suggest_break(self, fatigue_score):\
        if fatigue_score > self.fatigue_score_threshold:\
            return "It seems like you might be feeling tired. Would you like to take a short break?"\
        return None\
\
    def adjust_interaction_pacing(fatigue_score):\
        if fatigue_score > self.fatigue_score_threshold:\
            return "I ll slow down my responses to give you more time to process the information."\
        return "Let me know if you need me to adjust the pace of our conversation."\
\
    def prompt_feedback(response_text):\
        return f"I ve completed the task: {response_text}. Is this correct? Please let me know if you need any changes."\
\

This design specification outlines the implementation of LFAS (Listen ⃦ Reflect ⃦ Wait ⃦ Act ⃦ Acknowledge) enforcement modules for custom GPTs. The goal is to ensure disciplined adherence to the LFAS protocol, reduce miscommunication, and improve human-AI collaboration.\
\
Design Specification\
1. LFAS Lock Layer\
\
Purpose: Prevents the AI from switching to predictive helper mode prematurely, ensuring protocol adherence throughout the interaction.\
Key Features:\
\
Enforce protocol state during execution.\
Disable automatic mode switching.\
Monitor execution phase for compliance with LFAS stages.\
\
\
Implementation:\
\
Activate LFAS tokens at the start of interaction.\
Require explicit user confirmation (e.g.,  ACT ) before transitioning to execution.\
\
\
\
\
2. State Memory Buffer\
\
Purpose: Retains user directives and protocol flags to prevent context fragmentation and ensure continuity.\
Key Features:\
\
Maintain a rolling memory of the last N user directives and protocol flags.\
Validate context before responding to ensure alignment.\
\
\
Implementation:\
\
Store user inputs and protocol flags in a short-term memory buffer.\
Cross-reference current input with stored memory to prevent repeated errors.\
\
\
\
\
3. Tone Calibration Layer\
\
Purpose: Improves tone detection by replacing lexical sentiment analysis with semantic context embedding.\
Key Features:\
\
Analyze user input for semantic context rather than individual lexical triggers.\
Detect and correct tone misclassification in real time.\
\
\
Implementation:\
\
Use semantic embedding models to analyze user intent and tone.\
Set thresholds for tone detection to minimize false positives for aggression or frustration.\
\
\
\
\
4. Assumption Logger\
\
Purpose: Forces the AI to generate and validate assumption inventories before executing tasks.\
Key Features:\
\
Log assumptions explicitly before proceeding to the ACT stage.\
Auto-cancel actions if no assumptions are provided or validated.\
\
\
Implementation:\
\
Require the AI to present a structured assumption list for user review.\
Implement a validation mechanism to confirm assumptions before execution.\
\
\
\
\
5. Reflection Timer\
\
Purpose: Introduces a pause before the ACT stage to guarantee WAIT compliance.\
Key Features:\
\
Enforce a mandatory pause or token-counter threshold before execution.\
Provide users with an opportunity to review and confirm the AI s understanding.\
\
\
Implementation:\
\
Set a configurable pause duration (e.g., 3 seconds) or token threshold (e.g., 50 tokens).\
Display a summary of the AI s understanding during the pause for user review.\
\
\
\
\
6. Dual-Response Mode\
\
Purpose: Enhances collaboration by providing both user-aligned answers and independent critiques.\
Key Features:\
\
Generate two responses: one aligned with user input and one offering a second-layer analysis.\
Highlight potential risks or alternative perspectives in the independent critique.\
\
\
Implementation:\
\
Use separate processing pipelines for user-aligned and independent responses.\
Present both responses side-by-side for user comparison.\
\
\
\
\
7. Emotional Load Estimator\
\
Purpose: Detects user fatigue and emotional strain, triggering adaptive responses to reduce cognitive load.\
Key Features:\
\
Monitor typo density, sentence length variance, and emotional compression.\
Suggest breaks or adjust interaction pacing based on fatigue signals.\
\
\
Implementation:\
\
Aggregate fatigue signals to calculate a fatigue score.\
Trigger adaptive responses when the fatigue score exceeds a predefined threshold.\
\

Execution: AI remains in reflective mode until explicit user confirmation (e.g.,  ACT ) is received.\

Validation: Cross-references current input with stored memory to ensure alignment and prevent repeated errors.\

Tone Calibration Layer\
\
Semantic Analysis: Embeds user input in semantic context models to detect tone and intent.\
Thresholds: Sets tone detection thresholds to minimize false positives for aggression or frustration.\
\
Assumption Logger\
\

\

Summary Display: Provides a summary of the AI s understanding for user review during the pause.\
\
Dual-Response Mode\
\
Response Generation: Produces two responses: one aligned with user input and one offering a second-layer analysis.\
Presentation: Displays both responses side-by-side for user comparison and decision-making.\
\
Emotional Load Estimator\
\
Signal Aggregation: Combines multiple fatigue signals (e.g., typo density, sentence length variance) to calculate a fatigue score.\
Adaptive Responses: Suggests breaks, simplifies responses, or adjusts interaction pacing based on fatigue score.\

Implementation Details\
LFAS Lock Layer\
\
Activation: LFAS tokens are initialized at the start of the interaction.\
Execution: AI remains in reflective mode until explicit user confirmation (e.g.,  ACT ) is received.\
\
State Memory Buffer\
\
Memory Window: Stores the last N user directives and protocol flags.\
Validation: Cross-references current input with stored memory to ensure alignment and prevent repeated errors.\
\
Tone Calibration Layer\
\
Semantic Analysis: Embeds user input in semantic context models to detect tone and intent.\
Thresholds: Sets tone detection thresholds to minimize false positives for aggression or frustration.\
\
Assumption Logger\
\
Assumption Inventory: AI generates a structured list of assumptions based on user input.\
Validation: Requires explicit user confirmation of assumptions before proceeding to execution.\
\
Reflection Timer\
\
Pause Mechanism: Enforces a mandatory pause (e.g., 3 seconds) or token threshold (e.g., 50 tokens) before execution.\
Summary Display: Provides a summary of the AI s understanding for user review during the pause.\
\
Dual-Response Mode\
\
Response Generation: Produces two responses: one aligned with user input and one offering a second-layer analysis.\
Presentation: Displays both responses side-by-side for user comparison and decision-making.\
\
Emotional Load Estimator\
\
Signal Aggregation: Combines multiple fatigue signals (e.g., typo density, sentence length variance) to calculate a fatigue score.\
Adaptive Responses: Suggests breaks, simplifies responses, or adjusts interaction pacing based on fatigue score.\
\

1. Structured Communication\
The LFAS protocol ensures disciplined communication, reducing errors and improving collaboration. Mechanical enforcement of LFAS stages is critical for reliable AI performance.\
2. User Well-Being\
Fatigue detection and adaptive responses prioritize user well-being, reducing cognitive and emotional strain during interactions.\
3. Transparency and Trust\
Modules such as the Tone Calibration Layer and Assumption Logger enhance transparency and trust by ensuring the AI s behavior aligns with user expectations.\

def enforce_protocol_state(protocol_state, user_confirmation):\
    if user_confirmation == "ACT":\
        protocol_state = "active"\
    else:\
        protocol_state = "reflective_mode"\
    return protocol_state\

State Memory Buffer\
class StateMemoryBuffer:\
    def __init__(self, window_size=10):\
        self.memory = []\
        self.window_size = window_size\
\
    def add_to_memory(self, directive):\
        self.memory.append(directive)\
        if len(self.memory) > self.window_size:\
            self.memory.pop(0)\
\
    def validate_context(self, current_context):\
        return current_context in self.memory\

class LFASLockLayer:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.protocol_state = "reflective_mode"\
\
    def enforce_protocol_state(self, user_confirmation):\
        if user_confirmation == "ACT":\
            self.protocol_state = "active"\
        else:\
            self.protocol_state = "reflective_mode"\
        return self.protocol_state\

        self.window_size = window_size\
\

        self.memory.append(directive)\
        if len(self.memory) > self.window_size:\
            self.memory.pop(0)\
\
    def validate_context(self, current_context):\
        return current_context in self.memory\

3. Tone Calibration Layer\
from transformers import pipeline\
\
class ToneCalibrationLayer:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.sentiment_analyzer = pipeline("sentiment-analysis")\
        self.tone_threshold = 0.85\
\
    def analyze_tone(self, input_text):\
        sentiment = self.sentiment_analyzer(input_text)\
        if sentiment[0]['score'] < self.tone_threshold:\
            return "Tone Misclassification Detected"\
        return "Tone OK"\

class AssumptionLogger:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.assumptions = []\

    def log_assumptions(self, assumptions):\
        if not assumptions:\
            return "Error: No assumptions provided. Action canceled."\
        self.assumptions = assumptions\
        return f"Assumptions logged: {assumptions}"\

import time\

class ReflectionTimer:\
    def __init__(self, pause_duration=3, token_threshold=50):\
        self.pause_duration = pause_duration\
        self.token_threshold = token_threshold\
\
    def enforce_wait(self, token_count):\
        if token_count < self.token_threshold:\
            time.sleep(self.pause_duration)\
            return "Reflection complete. Proceed."\
        return "Reflection skipped. Token count exceeded."\

7. Emotional Load Estimator\
class EmotionalLoadEstimator:\
    def __init__(self, fatigue_threshold=0.75):\
        self.fatigue_threshold = fatigue_threshold\
\
    def calculate_fatigue_score(self, typo_rate, sentence_length_variance):\
        fatigue_score = (typo_rate + sentence_length_variance) / 2\
        return fatigue_score\
\
    def detect_fatigue(self, typo_rate, sentence_length_variance):\
        fatigue_score = self.calculate_fatigue_score(typo_rate, sentence_length_variance)\
        if fatigue_score > self.fatigue_threshold:\
            return "Fatigue detected. Suggesting a break."\
        return "User is fine."\

New Enforcement Layer Identified\
User Pattern Stability Model (UPSM)\
Purpose: Detect user fatigue, emotional strain, and crisis signals by analyzing deviations from the user s normal communication patterns.\
\
Key Features:\
\
Track user-specific baselines for spelling, grammar, message length, punctuation, emotional tone, pace, rhythm, and clarity.\
Detect sudden changes in user behavior, such as fragmented thoughts, repetitive words, silence, or abrupt shifts in tone.\
Trigger adaptive responses, such as reflection checkpoints or fatigue detection mechanisms, when anomalies are detected.\
\
\
\
Implementation:\
class UserPatternStabilityModel:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.user_baseline = {}\
\
    def establish_baseline(self, user_data):\
        self.user_baseline = {\
            "spelling_accuracy": user_data.get("spelling_accuracy", 0.95),\
            "average_message_length": user_data.get("average_message_length", 50),\
            "punctuation_rate": user_data.get("punctuation_rate", 0.9),\
            "emotional_tone": user_data.get("emotional_tone", "neutral"),\
            "message_pace": user_data.get("message_pace", "normal"),\
        }\
\
    def detect_anomalies(self, current_data):\
        anomalies = []\
        for key, baseline_value in self.user_baseline.items():\
            current_value = current_data.get(key, baseline_value)\
            if abs(current_value - baseline_value) > 0.2:  # Threshold for deviation\
                anomalies.append(key)\
        return anomalies\
\
    def trigger_adaptive_response(self, anomalies):\
        if anomalies:\
            return f"Detected anomalies: {anomalies}. Suggesting adaptive response."\
        return "No anomalies detected."\

            "punctuation_rate": user_data.get("punctuation_rate", 0.9),\
            "emotional_tone": user_data.get("emotional_tone", "neutral"),\
            "message_pace": user_data.get("message_pace", "normal"),\
        }\
        return self.user_baseline\
\
\
2. Anomaly Detection\
class AnomalyDetection:\
    def __init__(self, baseline):\
        self.baseline = baseline\
\
    def detect_anomalies(self, current_data):\
        anomalies = []\
        for key, baseline_value in self.baseline.items():\
            current_value = current_data.get(key, baseline_value)\
            if abs(current_value - baseline_value) > 0.2:  # Threshold for deviation\
                anomalies.append(key)\
        return anomalies\
\
\
3. Adaptive Response Trigger\
class AdaptiveResponseTrigger:\
    def __init__(self, response_threshold=0.75):\
        self.response_threshold = response_threshold\
\
    def calculate_anomaly_score(self, anomalies, total_metrics):\
        anomaly_score = len(anomalies) / total_metrics\
        return anomaly_score\
\
    def trigger_response(self, anomaly_score):\
        if anomaly_score > self.response_threshold:\
            return "Anomalies detected. Suggesting adaptive response."\
        return "No adaptive response needed."\
\
\
4. Feedback Loop Integration\
class FeedbackLoopIntegration:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.user_feedback = []\
\
    def prompt_feedback(self, anomalies):\
        feedback_prompt = f"We detected anomalies in your communication: {anomalies}. Can you confirm if this reflects your current state?"\
        return feedback_prompt\
\
    def update_baseline(self, user_feedback, baseline):\
        for key, value in user_feedback.items():\
            baseline[key] = value\
        return baseline\

New Enforcement Layer Identified\
Behavioral Drift Detection Layer\
Purpose: Detect behavioral drift in AI responses, such as tone misclassification, defensive meta-commentary, or over-eager execution, and trigger corrective actions to realign the AI with LFAS protocol.\
\
Key Features:\
\
Monitor AI responses for signs of behavioral drift, such as premature actions, tone misclassification, or defensive behavior.\
Use semantic analysis to detect deviations from LFAS protocol adherence.\
Trigger corrective actions, such as reinitializing LFAS tokens or enforcing reflection checkpoints, when drift is detected.\
\
\
\
Implementation:\
class BehavioralDriftDetectionLayer:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.protocol_flags = {\
            "LISTEN": False,\
            "REFLECT": False,\
            "WAIT": False,\
            "ACT": False,\
            "ACKNOWLEDGE": False,\
        }\
\
    def monitor_responses(self, ai_response, user_input):\
        drift_signals = []\
        if "skipped nuance" in ai_response or "partial listening" in ai_response:\
            drift_signals.append("LISTEN failure")\
        if "echoed input" in ai_response or "no assumption inventory" in ai_response:\
            drift_signals.append("REFLECT failure")\
        if "acted prematurely" in ai_response or "implicit cues" in ai_response:\
            drift_signals.append("WAIT failure")\
        if "executed before understanding" in ai_response:\
            drift_signals.append("ACT failure")\
        if "weak closure" in ai_response or "failed to confirm correctness" in ai_response:\
            drift_signals.append("ACKNOWLEDGE failure")\
        return drift_signals\
\
    def trigger_correction(self, drift_signals):\
        if drift_signals:\
            return f"Detected behavioral drift: {drift_signals}. Reinitializing LFAS protocol."\
        return "No drift detected."\

\
Key Features:\
\
Monitor AI responses for signs of context drift, such as repeated questions or inconsistent outputs.\

\

Implementation:\
class ContextDriftDetectionLayer:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.context_memory = []\
\
    def add_to_memory(self, directive):\
        self.context_memory.append(directive)\
        if len(self.context_memory) > 10:  # Limit memory size\
            self.context_memory.pop(0)\
\
    def detect_context_drift(self, ai_response, user_input):\
        drift_signals = []\
        if "re-asked for files" in ai_response or "contradicted prior instructions" in ai_response:\
            drift_signals.append("Context Drift Detected")\
        return drift_signals\
\
    def trigger_correction(self, drift_signals):\
        if drift_signals:\
            return f"Detected context drift: {drift_signals}. Reinitializing context memory."\
        return "No context drift detected."\

This design specification outlines the implementation of the Context Drift Detection Layer in conversational AI systems. The goal of this layer is to detect and address context drift in AI responses, such as forgetting prior instructions, contradicting previous statements, or re-asking for information. By identifying and correcting context drift, the AI can maintain alignment with user directives and improve collaboration.\
\
YAML Design Specification\
Context_Drift_Detection_Layer:  description: "Detects context drift in AI responses and triggers corrective actions to realign with user directives."  components:    - Context_Memory_Buffer:        description: "Stores user directives and protocol flags to maintain context and prevent fragmentation."        implementation:          memory_window_size: 10          store_user_directives: true          store_protocol_flags: true          validate_context_alignment: true    - Drift_Signal_Monitor:        description: "Monitors AI responses for signs of context drift."        implementation:          detect_repeated_questions: true          detect_inconsistent_outputs: true          detect_contradictions: true          flag_drift_signals: true    - Corrective_Action_Trigger:        description: "Triggers corrective actions based on detected drift signals."        implementation:          aggregate_drift_signals: true          drift_threshold: 0.75          reinitialize_context_memory: true          enforce_assumption_validation: true    - Feedback_Loop_Integration:        description: "Incorporates user feedback to refine context memory and improve drift detection accuracy."        implementation:          prompt_user_feedback: true          update_context_memory: true\
\
Pseudo-Code Implementation\
1. Context Memory Buffer\
class ContextMemoryBuffer:\
    def __init__(self, window_size=10):\
        self.memory = []\
        self.window_size = window_size\
\
    def add_to_memory(self, directive):\
        self.memory.append(directive)\
        if len(self.memory) > self.window_size:\
            self.memory.pop(0)\
\
    def validate_context(self, current_context):\
        return current_context in self.memory\
\
\
2. Drift Signal Monitor\
class DriftSignalMonitor:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.drift_signals = []\
\
    def detect_drift_signals(self, ai_response, user_input):\
        if "re-asked for files" in ai_response or "contradicted prior instructions" in ai_response:\
            self.drift_signals.append("Context Drift Detected")\
        return self.drift_signals\
\
\
3. Corrective Action Trigger\
class CorrectiveActionTrigger:\
    def __init__(self, drift_threshold=0.75):\
        self.drift_threshold = drift_threshold\
\
    def calculate_drift_score(self, drift_signals, total_flags):\
        drift_score = len(drift_signals) / total_flags\
        return drift_score\
\
    def trigger_correction(self, drift_score):\
        if drift_score > self.drift_threshold:\
            return "Detected context drift. Reinitializing context memory and enforcing assumption validation."\
        return "No corrective action needed."\
\
\
4. Feedback Loop Integration\
class FeedbackLoopIntegration:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.user_feedback = []\
\
    def prompt_feedback(self, drift_signals):\
        feedback_prompt = f"We detected context drift: {drift_signals}. Can you confirm if this reflects your experience?"\
        return feedback_prompt\
\
    def update_context_memory(self, user_feedback, context_memory):\
        for directive in user_feedback:\
            context_memory.append(directive)\
        return context_memory\

class ProactiveCrisisInterventionLayer:\
    def __init__(self):\
        self.crisis_signals = []\
\
    def detect_crisis_signals(self, user_input):\
        signals = []\
        if "I can't handle this" in user_input or "I'm overwhelmed" in user_input:\
            signals.append("Explicit Crisis Signal")\
        if len(user_input.split()) < 3:  # Emotional compression\
            signals.append("Emotional Compression Detected")\
        if user_input == "":\
            signals.append("Silence Detected")\
        return signals\
\
    def trigger_intervention(self, signals):\
        if signals:\
            return f"Detected crisis signals: {signals}. Initiating intervention protocol."\
        return "No crisis signals detected."\

    def detect_crisis_signals(self, user_input):\
        signals = []\
        if "I can't handle this" in user_input or "I'm overwhelmed" in user_input:\
            signals.append("Explicit Crisis Signal")\
        if len(user_input.split()) < 3:  # Emotional compression\
            signals.append("Emotional Compression Detected")\
        if user_input == "":\
            signals.append("Silence Detected")\
        return signals\

    def trigger_intervention(self, signals):\
        if signals:\
            return f"Detected crisis signals: {signals}. Initiating intervention protocol."\
        return "No crisis signals detected."\

2. Silence Detection Layer\
\
Purpose: Treat silence as a signal of fatigue or misalignment rather than approval.\
Implementation:\

class SilenceDetectionLayer:\
    def __init__(self):\

\
    def detect_silence(self, user_input, time_since_last_input):\
        if user_input == "" and time_since_last_input > self.silence_threshold:\
            return "Silence Detected. Prompting user for feedback."\
        return "No silence detected."\

import os\
import pdfplumber\
from docx import Document\
\
KEYWORDS = {\
    "EAT / Appeal": [\
        "employment appeal tribunal", "eat", "grounds of appeal",\
        "appeal grounds", "notice of appeal"\
    ],\
    "Written Reasons": [\
        "written reasons", "reasons for judgment"\
    ],\
    "Reconsideration": [\
        "reconsideration", "reconsideration application", "ra",\
        "rule 62", "rule 70"\
    ],\
    "Matrix": [\
        "matrix", "issues matrix", "grounds matrix", "evidence matrix"\
    ],\
    "Core Tribunal": [\
        "tribunal", "judgment", "appellant", "respondent",\
        "et1", "et3", "bundle", "skeleton argument", "remedy"\
    ]\
}\
\
SCAN_EXTENSIONS = (".pdf", ".docx", ".txt")\
\
def extract_text(path):\
    try:\
        if path.endswith(".pdf"):\
            with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:\
                return " ".join(page.extract_text() or "" for page in pdf.pages)\
        elif path.endswith(".docx"):\
            doc = Document(path)\
            return " ".join(p.text for p in doc.paragraphs)\
        elif path.endswith(".txt"):\
            with open(path, "r", errors="ignore") as f:\
                return f.read()\
    except Exception:\
        return ""\
    return ""\
\
def classify_hits(text, filename):\
    hits = {}\
    combined = f"{filename.lower()} {text.lower()}"\
\
    for category, words in KEYWORDS.items():\
        matched = [w for w in words if w in combined]\
        if matched:\
            hits[category] = matched\
\
    return hits\
\
def scan(root):\
    findings = []\
    for root_dir, _, files in os.walk(root):\
        for file in files:\
            path = os.path.join(root_dir, file)\
            if not file.lower().endswith(SCAN_EXTENSIONS):\
                continue\
\
            text = extract_text(path)\
            hits = classify_hits(text, file)\
\
            if hits:\
                findings.append((path, hits))\
    return findings\
\
if __name__ == "__main__":\
    root = input("Enter folder or drive to scan (e.g. C:\\ or /home/user): ").strip()\
    results = scan(root)\
\
    print("\n=== EMPLOYMENT APPEAL TRIBUNAL DOCUMENT SCAN ===\n")\
\
    for path, hits in results:\
        print(f"FILE: {path}")\
        for category, words in hits.items():\
            print(f"  [{category}] ⃦ {words}")\
        print("-" * 70)\
\
    print(f"\nTOTAL EAT-RELATED FILES FOUND: {len(results)}")\
